Where it began

Naseem Shah was born on 15 February 2003 and grew up in the town of Mayar Jandool, in Lower Dir in the north-west of Pakistan. Like many young cricketers, he started out with a taped tennis ball before his uncle took him to Lahore at 13 and enrolled him at the Abdul Qadir Cricket Academy, where Sulaman Qadir coached him.

Things moved fast after that. He was picked for Lahore Under-16s at 13 and Pakistan Under-16s at 14, and in September 2018 he played his first first-class match, for Zarai Taraqiati Bank Limited. Fast bowling runs in the family: his younger brothers Hunain and Ubaid are both quick bowlers, Hunain at first-class level and Ubaid for Pakistan at the 2024 Under-19 World Cup.

The player

His Test debut came against Australia on 21 November 2019, when he was 16, making him, at the time, the ninth-youngest player to appear in a Test. He reached 147 km/h in his very first over. A month later, against Sri Lanka, he took his first five-wicket haul at 16 years and 307 days; no fast bowler had ever done it younger. Then, in February 2020 against Bangladesh, he took a hat-trick at 16 years and 359 days, younger than anyone had ever done it in a Test.

By November 2026 he had played 20 Tests, taking 60 wickets at 35.13 with a best of 5 for 31. He went on to play one-day and T20 cricket for Pakistan too, and was part of the side that reached the final of the 2022 T20 World Cup.

What made him special

Pace and a lovely, smooth action were the gifts. Senior fast bowlers such as Waqar Younis admired him from his first Test, and experienced batsmen found him awkward from the start.

His batting was more modest, with 144 Test runs at 7.58, but he picked his moment. At the 2022 Asia Cup, with Pakistan in trouble against Afghanistan, he hit two sixes to win the game and send his side into the final. There are batsmen with far better averages who have never done that.

Away from the middle

He took his bowling around the world: Quetta Gladiators and Islamabad United in the Pakistan Super League, Gloucestershire in county cricket, and he signed for Welsh Fire in The Hundred. In 2021 he took two important wickets in the Caribbean Premier League final to help St Kitts and Nevis Patriots win their first title. In February 2026 he joined the Rawalpindi side in the PSL's first-ever auction.

And finally

Most people at 16 are worrying about exams. Naseem was bowling at 147 km/h to Australian batsmen, which is a different kind of test altogether.
